title: Deterministic tenant-sharded ingest with correlation-id TTL and reorder buffer
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As traffic grows, we see bursts from multi-tenant sources that lead to out-of-order writes, duplicated correlation IDs across tenants, and expensive reindexing in downstream systems. Current ingest path has a single hot partition for certain tenants and no deterministic routing based on event semantics, which causes variable tail latency for Loki/ELK writes and makes tracing joins brittle.

Goal: Implement an ingest shim that deterministically shards tenant events into stable logical partitions, enriches events with a canonical correlation fingerprint and TTL, and provides a small-ordering (reorder) buffer to repair minor out-of-order sequences. The component should emit structured JSON with canonical fields, surface backpressure signals for autoscaling, and integrate with both Loki label-based routing and Elasticsearch index templates.

Scope: This ticket covers: design and implementation of the shard key generation, correlation fingerprint/TTL, the reorder buffer (configurable window), schema normalization hooks, Loki label mapping, ES index template guidance, and rollout plus observability dashboards and alerts. End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout plan included. Does not include long-term archival/compaction changes (future ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic shard key computed from: tenant_id + hashed(source_uuid) with seed rotation support
Correlation fingerprint field (corr_fp) present on all structured logs; value stable for a request and expires after configurable TTL
Reorder buffer repairs sequences for up to 2s window (configurable) with metrics showing reorder rate <= 0.1% under normal load
Loki write client uses tenant and corr_fp as labels; ES ingestion uses tenant as index prefix and corr_fp as ingest_field
Backpressure metric emitted (ingest_queue_depth, reorder_shed_count) and alert when queue_depth > 75th percentile configured SLO
End-to-end tests demonstrate no data loss for restart scenarios and deterministic routing across 10k synthetic tenants
Canary rollout completes with no significant increase to tokenized per-request latency (<= +6ms p95)
implementation_notes: Shard key: tenant_id || ':' || trunc64(hmac_sha256(seed, source_uuid)) -> then consistent-hash to N logical shards per region
Seed rotation: maintain dual-hash window to rehash gracefully over deployment; migration runbook will move keys over time using a small shadow writing period

Corr_fp generation: canonicalize request-level trace_id if present; else fallback to sha1(method+path+client_ip+approx_timestamp) truncated to 128 bits; attach corr_fp_ttl epoch (ISO8601 expiration) in event metadata

Reorder buffer: in-memory ring-buffer per shard keyed by sequence_number (if present) or arrival_time; hold up to 2s by default or N events; aggressively shed when memory high and emit reorder_shed_count metric

Schema normalization: pluggable adapters that map incoming keys to canonical set (timestamp, level, tenant_id, service, corr_fp, corr_fp_ttl, trace_id, span_id, message, attributes). Adapters for common sources (envoy, nginx, java-logback, node-winston) included
Loki integration: preferred labels [tenant, service, corr_fp]; push via loki-push with batch_size tuning; prefer multiline=false and structured_json payloads for query efficiency

ES integration: write to index <tenant>-logs-YYYY.MM.DD; provide sample index template with mappings: corr_fp keyword, trace_id keyword, timestamp date, attributes flattened object; set refresh_interval to 30s for heavy tenants

Backpressure: expose /metrics for prometheus (ingest_queue_depth_gauge, reorder_buffer_size, reorder_shed_count, shard_hotspot_ratio). Build autoscaler hook that reads ingest_queue_depth_gauge per shard
Tracing hooks: add span start/finish around the ingest shim; attach internal span tags (shard_id, corr_fp, reorder_delay_ms) for latency debugging
Security: redact PII keys in attributes adapter; consult compliance before adding any raw payload forwarding to ES (security_review_required=true)
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit/integration tests (local Loki/ES) -> PR to main
2) Deploy binary behind feature flag (ingest_shim.v2) to non-prod cluster; shadow write for 24h comparing keys and corr_fp distribution
3) Canary: enable deterministic routing for 5% of traffic (selected tenants) with full write to Loki and ES; monitor reorder_rate, p95 latency, write error rate
4) Expand to 25% then 50% over 48h if metrics stable, run drift job to compare index counts and corr_fp collision rate
5) Flip default for all tenants; deprecate legacy hot-partition routing after 2 weeks of stable metrics
6) Post-mortem + checklist items: seed rotation runbook, operator script to recompute shard mapping for orphaned events
testing_plan: Unit tests for shard hashing and seed rotation behavior (edge seeds, collisions)
Deterministic property tests: identical input -> same shard across 1000 iterations
Load test: 50k events/sec with 10k tenants in k8s perf env; assert reorder_rate < 0.2% and no data loss on pod restart
Chaos test: kill ingest worker mid-buffer; verify restart replays buffer and emits missing metrics; validate idempotence in downstream ES and Loki (use dedup svc)
Integration: end-to-end smoke with trace join: generate trace -> ensure all logs with same corr_fp surface in Grafana trace panel
Canary validation job: nightly job that compares counts between legacy and new path for canary tenants and flags >0.5% divergence
